text:
maria: Starting bring-up for mn-lakes1 GPU pool (new MN region). Plan: 8x A100-80GB spot nodes, initial bootstrap now. tagging @jonathan for handoff and oncall verification. following runbook /runbooks/region-bootstrap.
jonathan: ack — I'll watch health checks and routing. share any early failures here.
kevin: terraform apply failing on capacity step: looks like cloudquota error from provider.
sasha: can you paste the snippet?
maria: ```
Error: QuotaExceeded: Requested accelerators (GPUs) 8 but allowed 4 in project
  on modules/gpu_pool/main.tf line 42, in resource "cloud_gpu_pool":
  42: resource "cloud_gpu_pool" "default" {
```
sasha: ok — two quick options: request quota bump (slow) or start with 4 GPUs on-demand for validation. spots we can add later. FYI cost on-demand >> spot.
maria: running quick patch to reduce target to 4 for canary: `terraform apply -var="gpu_count=4" -auto-approve`
deploy-bot: tfapply started by maria at 1969739000
deploy-bot: tfapply completed with errors
deploy-bot: ERROR: attach eni failed: netlink error: RTNETLINK answers: File exists
kevin: that netlink/ENI error usually correlates with CNI/MTU mismatch during ENI attach. also seeing kubelet init errors on driver installer on a node:
```
[init] running driver install
make: gcc: Command not found
ERROR: nvidia-module-build failed
```
chris: gcc missing in AMI -> driver build container exits and node stays NotReady. For ENI/netlink, check Calico MTU vs ENI MTU, and any duplicate iptables/netplan scripts from cloud-init.
maria: rolling back TF to previous state for now and marking this bring-up blocked. will patch AMI to include build deps and test smaller canary on on-demand. :thumbsup:
jonathan: handoff to eng-sre: please add temporary alerts: GPU allocation failures, driver-install CrashLoop, and node kernel taint. Also monitoring for ENI attach errors. Note on cost: running 1 on-demand A100 node is estimated ~ $700/day — confirm budget before extended testing.
sasha: I'll open the quota request with cloud provider and CC infra@redwood. putting autoscaling and large allocation on hold until quota bump or we limit to on-demand canary.
maria: next steps (assigned): 1) AMI fix — include gcc, make, kernel headers (@kevin) 2) Request accelerator quota -> target 16 GPUs (@sasha) 3) Re-run TF for canary with gpu_count=4 on on-demand, validate network and mount ( @jonathan ) 4) If netlink/ENI persists, try lowering ENI MTU from 9001 -> 8900 and disable duplicate cloud-init net config ( @kevin + @chris ).
maria: tagging this thread for handoff and will update when AMI bake and quota ticket are in. keeping logs here for postmortem/launch checklist.
jonathan: ack — will prepare the rollout playbook changes and add canary rollback steps. last update please include the AMI id and tf plan output.
